summary: Nadler interprets intellectual love as active joy, virtue and freedom and reads the eternal aspect nonpersonally. His broadly harmonious account of rational sociality and vocabulary of a part remaining after death do not settle the primary text's difficult relation between eternal possession and temporal development.
